كَيْدٌ : see 1. ―
-b2- (tropical:) War: (S, K:) so called because of the stratagems employed therein. (TA.) One says, غَزَا فُلَانٌ فَلَمْ يَلْقَ كَيْدًا (tropical:) Such a one went on a hostile expedition and found not war: (S, L:) i. e., did not fight. (A.) ―
-b3- كَيْدٌ ذَاتُ غَدْرٍ (tropical:) A war characterized by perfidy. كيد is here made fem. because meaning حَرْبٌ. (L, from a trad.) ＝
-A2- كَيْدٌ Vomit. (S, * L, K. *) بَلَعَ الكَيْدَ. He swallowed vomit. (L, from a trad.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
